purpose: Teleon writes candidate code. This contract requires generated code to be graphable, scalable, and easy for LLMs to understand from the identifiers and contract metadata before formal type optimization.
naming_law: Generated Python identifiers must use meaningful location-derived names: py_<kind>_<file>__<scope>__<name>. Long names are intentional because AI reads the code and long names carry context.
typing_law: Defer strict parameter typing in the first generated draft. Prefer flexible scalar_or_sequence contracts and plain dict/list envelopes. Add stricter types after runtime shape, graph edges, and proof coverage stabilize during optimization.

rules.rule: Generated code and model-authored review are candidates. They must carry serves_truth=false until deterministic proofs and promotion gates pass.
Generated Python functions, classes, constants, module vars, args, and locals should be emitted in the py_<kind>_<file>__<scope>__<name> convention from the start.
Generated code must carry purpose, input shape, output shape, dependencies, and proof-to-run either in a contract object or docstring.
Any generated step that might later process multiple records should accept scalar_or_sequence input via normalize_to_sequence or a lifted scalar step.
Iteration must use an explicit bounded loop contract with max_iterations and history. Unbounded while loops are not acceptable generated-code defaults.
Repeated branch chains should become dispatch tables or rule rows so adding a case means adding data, not rewriting control logic.
Numbered scalar series like item1/item2/item3, threshold_a/threshold_b, or duplicated adjacent calls should be rewritten to arrays, maps, or rule tables.
The generated block is not promotable until py_compile or AST parse, pyprefix graph/audit, relevant contract checks, and the registered proof gate pass.

benefits: LLMs can infer purpose from names without reading whole files.
Deterministic graph tools can trace calls, data movement, and operation nodes.
Scalar prototypes can scale to batch processing without rewriting the core function.
Magic values, fragile branch chains, and copy-paste repeated calls become queryable graph smells.
Formal types can be added later from observed stable contracts instead of guessed upfront.
